en: be published; be printed; appear (in a paper, magazine or site)

examples.en: My article was published in the newspaper.
I'm waiting for the day my photo appears in the magazine.

examples.ko: 광고가 게재되면 문의 전화가 많이 와요.
examples.en: Once the ad runs, we get lots of calls.
I was happy that my reader's letter got printed.
This article was posted on the website yesterday.
The paper is scheduled to be published in the journal.

explain: 게재되다는 글, 광고, 사진이 신문이나 잡지, 누리집에 실릴 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '실리다'가 더 자연스럽고, 게재되다는 기사나 공지 같은 딱딱한 글에서 많이 나와요. 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '게재하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 게재되다 is used when a text, photo or ad appears in a newspaper, magazine or website. In everyday speech Koreans say 실리다 more often; 게재되다 sounds formal and shows up in news and notices. The active partner is 게재하다.

en: publish; run; print (an article, ad or photo)

examples.en: The newspaper published a reader's piece.
I'll post the notice on our website.
You need permission if you want to publish a photo.

examples.ko: 잡지에 광고를 게재하는 데 비용이 얼마나 들어요?
examples.en: How much does it cost to run an ad in a magazine?
The editor printed my story for me.

examples.ko: 오류가 있어서 기사를 다시 게재하기로 했어요.
examples.en: There was an error, so we decided to run the article again.

explain: 게재하다는 글, 광고, 사진을 신문이나 인터넷에 싣는 일에 써서 공지, 기사, 광고 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 말할 때는 인터넷이면 '올리다', 신문·잡지면 '싣다'를 더 많이 써요. 보통 '~에 ~을/를 게재하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 게재하다 is used for putting an article, ad or photo in a newspaper or online, so it appears mostly around notices, news and ads. In speech people say 올리다 for online and 싣다 for print. The usual pattern is ~에 ~을/를 게재하다.

en: advise; urge; recommend (officially)

examples.en: The doctor advised me to exercise.
The government urges people to wear masks indoors.

examples.ko: 회사에서 일찍 퇴근하라고 권고했는데도 다들 남았어요.
examples.en: The company urged everyone to leave early, but they all stayed.

examples.ko: 전문가들이 물을 자주 마시라고 권고하고 있어요.
examples.en: Experts recommend drinking water often.

examples.ko: 선생님이 한 번 쉬어 보라고 권고하셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher advised me to take a break.
The committee will recommend that the rule be changed.

explain: 권고하다는 정부, 의사, 기관이 '이렇게 하는 것이 좋다'고 공식적으로 말할 때 써요. 친구에게 추천할 때는 '추천하다'나 '권하다'를 써요. 강제는 아니라서 따르지 않아도 되지만 하는 편이 좋다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 권고하다 is for governments, doctors or institutions officially saying that something is advisable. To a friend you would say 추천하다 or 권하다. It is not an order: you may ignore it, but it is better to follow.

en: take effect; come into force

examples.en: The new law takes effect next month.
The contract came into force on the day it was signed.
Once the agreement takes effect, tariffs will go down.

examples.ko: 경보가 발효되는 동안에는 밖에 나가지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go outside while the warning is in effect.
This rule is set to take effect at midnight tomorrow.
A heat advisory went into effect, so we canceled the event.

explain: 발효되다는 법, 조약, 경보처럼 공식적인 것이 효력을 갖기 시작할 때 써요. 같은 소리의 '발효'는 김치나 된장이 익는 것도 가리키니 문장에서 구별하세요. '시행되다'는 실제로 실행되는 것에, 발효되다는 효력이 생기는 순간에 가까워요.
explain_en: 발효되다 is used when something official such as a law, treaty or warning starts to have effect. The same-sounding 발효 also means fermentation of kimchi or soybean paste, so tell them apart by context. 시행되다 stresses actual enforcement, while 발효되다 stresses the moment it becomes valid.

en: look rough or delinquent; rowdy; unruly

examples.en: That student's way of talking is a bit rough.
He looked at me with a rough, defiant face.
Even though he dresses like a tough kid, he has a kind heart.
The teacher worries when a child acts rowdy.

examples.ko: 동네에 불량스러운 아이들이 모여 있다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard some rough-looking kids hang out in the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 처음에 불량스러웠지만 나중에 변해요.
examples.en: The main character is unruly at first but changes later.

explain: 불량스럽다는 사람의 말투, 표정, 태도가 건들거리고 나빠 보일 때 써요. 실제로 나쁜 짓을 했는지보다 '그렇게 보인다'는 인상을 말할 때가 많아요. '불량하다'가 더 직접적이고 평가가 강해요.
explain_en: 불량스럽다 describes a person whose speech, face or attitude looks swaggering and bad. It is more about the impression ('he looks like trouble') than about actual misdeeds. 불량하다 is more direct and judgmental.

en: be inherited; be passed down by inheritance

examples.en: The house was passed down to the son.
The property is inherited equally by the children.
When the company passed to his daughter, its name changed.

examples.ko: 유언이 없으면 재산은 법에 따라 상속될 거예요.
examples.en: Without a will, the property will be inherited according to law.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 오래전에 할아버지께 상속된 거예요.
examples.en: This land was inherited from my grandfather long ago.
Tax is charged on inherited property.

explain: 상속되다는 재산이나 권리가 법에 따라 사람에게서 사람에게 넘어갈 때 써서 집, 땅, 회사 같은 대상과 함께 나와요. 성격이나 얼굴이 닮는 것은 '유전되다', 전통이 이어지는 것은 '전해지다'라고 해요. 받는 사람 쪽은 '상속받다'를 써요.
explain_en: 상속되다 is for property or rights passing legally from one person to another, so it goes with houses, land and companies. Looks and personality passed on are 유전되다, and traditions handed down are 전해지다. From the receiver's side you say 상속받다.

en: bequeath; pass on property as an inheritance (the receiver 'inherits')

examples.en: My father left the house to his son.

examples.ko: 재산을 누구에게 상속할지 아직 못 정했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided yet whom to leave the property to.

examples.ko: 할머니는 딸 셋에게 땅을 똑같이 상속하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother left the land equally to her three daughters.
You need documents to leave property by will.

examples.ko: 아버지가 저에게 가게를 상속하기 전에 빚을 모두 갚았어요.
examples.en: My father paid off all the debts before leaving the shop to me.
The chairman announced he would leave the company to his son.

explain: 상속하다는 재산을 물려주는 사람이 주어이고, 받는 사람에게는 '에게/께'를 붙여요. 받는 사람이 주어일 때는 '상속받다'를 써요. 말할 때는 '물려주다'가 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: In 상속하다 the subject is the person leaving the property, and the receiver takes 에게 or 께. When the receiver is the subject, use 상속받다. In casual talk 물려주다 sounds softer.

en: be shortened; be reduced

examples.en: The construction period was shortened by two months.

examples.ko: 새 도로가 생기면서 출근 시간이 단축돼요.
examples.en: With the new road, my commute gets shorter.

examples.ko: 수업 시간이 단축되는 바람에 숙제가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Class got shortened, so the homework was reduced.

examples.ko: 줄이 짧아서 기다리는 시간이 많이 단축됐어요.
examples.en: The line was short, so the waiting time was cut a lot.

examples.ko: 근무 시간이 단축되면 저녁에 운동할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If working hours are shortened, I can exercise in the evening.
The cost dropped as much as the distance was cut.

explain: 단축되다는 시간, 거리, 기간처럼 길이가 있는 것이 짧아질 때 써요. 숫자나 가격이 줄 때는 '줄어들다', '감소하다'를 써요. 사람이 줄이면 '단축하다', 저절로 짧아지면 '단축되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: 단축되다 is for things with length, such as time, distance or a period, getting shorter. For numbers or prices going down, use 줄어들다 or 감소하다. When someone shortens it on purpose it is 단축하다; when it just becomes shorter, 단축되다.

en: be added; be attached (on top of something)

examples.en: Tax is added to the price.
New content was added to the explanation.

examples.ko: 기본 요금에 서비스 요금이 부가되는 가게도 있어요.
examples.en: Some stores add a service charge on top of the base price.

examples.ko: 이 상품에는 특별한 기능이 부가되어 있어요.
examples.en: This product comes with an extra feature added.

examples.ko: 점수에 보너스가 부가되면 순위가 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: If a bonus is added to the score, the ranking will change.
I marked the added items in red.

explain: 부가되다는 이미 있는 것 위에 따로 더해질 때 써요. '부가 가치세', '부가 서비스'처럼 앞에 붙는 말로도 자주 나와요. '추가되다'는 목록에 하나 더 들어가는 느낌이고, 부가되다는 본체에 딸려 붙는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 부가되다 is used when something is added separately on top of what already exists. The form 부가 shows up in words like 부가 가치세 (VAT) and 부가 서비스. 추가되다 feels like one more item in a list, while 부가되다 feels like something attached to the main thing.

en: add; attach (on top of something)

examples.en: I added one example to the basic explanation.
We are trying to add a new feature to the product.
How much is it if tax is added to the price?

examples.ko: 부가하는 말이 너무 길면 읽기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to read when the added remarks are too long.
I explained by adding the reason to the sentence.
I'll add one more service for you.

explain: 부가하다는 '붙여서 더하다'는 느낌이 강한 글말이에요. 파일을 붙여 보낼 때는 '첨부하다'를 쓰니 헷갈리지 마세요. 말할 때는 보통 '덧붙이다'나 '더하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 부가하다 is a written-style word with a strong sense of attaching something on top. When sending a file with an email, the word is 첨부하다, so do not mix them up. In speech people usually say 덧붙이다 or 더하다.

en: be settled; be brought under control; be sorted out

examples.en: I'm glad the accident was dealt with quickly.
It takes time until the confusion is sorted out.
Only after the fight was settled did everyone smile.
The problem wasn't resolved, so the meeting dragged on.
I'll contact you as soon as things are under control.
It was a big mistake, but it was handled well.

explain: 수습되다는 어지럽거나 문제가 된 일이 정리되어 가라앉을 때 써요. 사고, 소동, 논란처럼 일이 터진 뒤의 말과 잘 어울려요. 소리가 같은 '수습 사원'의 수습은 다른 말이니 따로 외우세요.
explain_en: 수습되다 is used when a messy or troublesome situation gets sorted out and calms down. It pairs with accidents, commotions and controversies, that is, things after trouble has broken out. The 수습 in 수습 사원 (trainee) sounds the same but is a different word.

en: make something shrink; cause to contract

examples.en: Cold makes metal contract.
When you contract your muscles, you use strength.
They say cold water constricts blood vessels.

examples.ko: 냉각 장치가 부품을 수축시켜서 꼭 맞게 만들었어요.
examples.en: The cooling device shrank the part so it fits tightly.
I heard the medicine has the effect of constricting blood vessels.

examples.ko: 운동 전에 근육을 수축시켰다 풀어 주세요.
examples.en: Before exercising, contract your muscles and then release them.

explain: 수축시키다는 어떤 힘이나 조건이 다른 것을 줄어들게 한다고 말할 때 써서 과학이나 건강 이야기에 주로 나와요. 스스로 줄어드는 것은 '수축하다/수축되다', 반대는 '팽창시키다'예요. 옷이 물에 줄어드는 일상 상황에서는 '줄다'를 써요.
explain_en: 수축시키다 says that some force or condition makes something shrink, so it appears mostly in science and health talk. Shrinking by itself is 수축하다 or 수축되다, and the opposite is 팽창시키다. For clothes that shrink in water, everyday Korean uses 줄다.

en: be constructed; be carried out (construction work)

examples.en: This building was built last year.
The new bridge will be built next year.
The floor was installed wrongly, so water collects.
Please check whether it was built according to the plan.

examples.ko: 도로가 시공되는 동안 차를 돌려서 다녀요.
examples.en: While the road is being built, we take a detour.

examples.ko: 시공된 지 십 년이 넘은 아파트예요.
examples.en: It's an apartment built more than ten years ago.

explain: 시공되다는 건물, 도로, 인테리어 공사가 현장에서 실제로 이루어질 때 써요. 설계는 도면 위의 계획이고 시공은 현장에서 짓는 일이라, '시공 업체'처럼 인테리어 이야기에서 자주 들려요. 일상에서 집을 지을 때는 '짓다'를 써요.
explain_en: 시공되다 is used when building, road or interior work is actually carried out on site. Design is the plan on paper and 시공 is the work on site, so you often hear 시공 업체 (contractor) in interior talk. In everyday speech, building a house is 짓다.

en: sting; ache sharply; (of taste) be pungent

examples.en: After eating spicy food, my tongue stings.
My chest ached whenever I thought of the breakup.
The antiseptic on the wound stings and burns.

examples.ko: 눈이 아린 걸 보니 양파 때문인가 봐요.
examples.en: My eyes sting, so it must be the onion.

examples.ko: 그 노래를 들으면 마음이 아려 와요.
examples.en: Hearing that song makes my heart ache.
The cold wind made the tip of my nose sting with cold.

explain: 아리다는 매운 것이나 상처, 찬바람에 닿았을 때의 쓰라림과 슬플 때 가슴이 저릿한 느낌에 모두 써요. '쓰리다'와 비슷하지만 아리다는 날카롭게 스며드는 느낌이에요. '가슴이 아리다'는 조금 문학적인 표현이에요.
explain_en: 아리다 covers both the stinging of spicy food, wounds or cold wind and the pang in the chest when sad. It is close to 쓰리다, but 아리다 feels sharper, as if it seeps in. 가슴이 아리다 sounds a bit literary.

en: decline; deteriorate; drop

examples.en: Stamina declines as you get older.
I'm worried because my grades keep dropping.
When you lack sleep, your concentration tends to decline.
The temperature dropped suddenly and my condition got worse.
We exchange products whose quality has declined.

examples.ko: 학습 의욕이 저하되는 시기가 누구에게나 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has a time when their motivation to study drops.

explain: 저하되다는 능력, 성적, 품질, 의욕, 면역력처럼 좋아야 하는 수준이 내려갈 때 써요. 온도나 가격이 내려가는 일에는 '떨어지다', '내려가다'를 써요. 원인이 있어 낮아지게 하는 쪽은 '저하시키다'예요.
explain_en: 저하되다 is used when a level that ought to be good goes down, such as ability, grades, quality, motivation or immunity. For temperature or price going down use 떨어지다 or 내려가다. The causative form is 저하시키다.

en: lower; reduce; worsen

examples.en: Noise lowers work performance.
They say stress weakens immunity.
A bad posture reduced my concentration.
We are looking for what lowers the quality.

examples.ko: 약이 판단력을 저하시킬 수 있으니 조심하세요.
examples.en: The medicine can impair judgment, so be careful.
Unnecessary features slowed it down, so I deleted them.

explain: 저하시키다는 어떤 원인이 수준이나 능력을 낮출 때 써요. 주어에는 사람보다 '소음, 스트레스, 피로, 나쁜 습관' 같은 원인이 많이 와요. 같은 뜻으로 '떨어뜨리다'는 말하기에 더 편해요.
explain_en: 저하시키다 is used when some cause lowers a level or ability. The subject is more often a cause such as noise, stress, fatigue or a bad habit than a person. 떨어뜨리다 means much the same and is easier to say in speech.

en: be thwarted; be dashed; fall through

examples.en: My dream fell through and I had a hard time for a while.
The plan was ruined by sudden rain.
After the negotiation collapsed, the mood turned bad.

examples.ko: 시험에 한 번 떨어졌다고 도전이 좌절된 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Failing an exam once does not mean the challenge is over.

examples.ko: 좌절되는 일이 있어도 다시 시작하면 돼요.
examples.en: Even if things fall through, you can start again.

examples.ko: 그의 첫 번째 시도는 자금 부족으로 좌절되었어요.
examples.en: His first attempt fell through due to a lack of funds.

explain: 좌절되다는 계획, 희망, 시도가 도중에 막혀 이루어지지 않을 때 써요. 사람의 마음이 꺾이는 것은 '좌절하다', 일이 막히는 것은 '좌절되다'예요. 일상에서는 '무산되다'도 가까운 말이에요.
explain_en: 좌절되다 is used when a plan, hope or attempt is blocked midway and does not come true. When a person's spirit breaks it is 좌절하다; when the matter itself is blocked it is 좌절되다. In daily talk 무산되다 is also close.

en: frustrate; thwart; dash (hopes); crush

examples.en: Repeated failure frustrates people.

examples.ko: 심한 비가 우리의 등산 계획을 좌절시켰어요.
examples.en: Heavy rain ruined our hiking plan.

examples.ko: 상대 팀이 우리 팀의 우승 희망을 좌절시켜서 아쉬웠어요.
examples.en: It was a pity that the other team crushed our hopes of winning.

examples.ko: 선생님은 학생을 좌절시키는 말을 하지 않으려고 해요.
examples.en: The teacher tries not to say things that discourage students.

examples.ko: 계속된 거절이 그의 의욕을 좌절시킬 수도 있어요.
examples.en: Continued rejection could crush his motivation.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 사고가 그의 꿈을 좌절시켰다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a sudden accident shattered his dream.

explain: 좌절시키다는 사람의 희망이나 계획, 의욕을 꺾는 원인이 주어로 와요. 말할 때는 '꺾다'가 더 흔하고, 좌절시키다는 기사나 글에서 많이 나와요. 그 결과 느끼는 마음은 '좌절감'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 좌절시키다 takes the cause that breaks someone's hope, plan or motivation as its subject. In speech 꺾다 is more common, while 좌절시키다 appears often in articles and writing. The feeling that results is called 좌절감.

en: be started; get under way

examples.en: The new construction gets under way next week.
A week has passed since the investigation began.
Once the project starts, the team will get busy.
The recovery work began right away yesterday.
When the investigation began, people took notice.
There is only a plan; work hasn't begun yet.

explain: 착수되다는 공사, 조사, 수사, 연구처럼 큰일이 실제로 시작될 때 써요. '시작되다'보다 격식이 있고 공식적인 일에 어울려요. 파티나 수업이 시작될 때는 '시작되다'를 써요. 시작하는 쪽은 '착수하다'예요.
explain_en: 착수되다 is used when a sizable job such as construction, an investigation or research actually begins. It is more formal than 시작되다 and suits official matters. For a party or a class starting, use 시작되다. The active form is 착수하다.

en: be satisfied; be met; be fulfilled

examples.en: I'll contact you right away once the application conditions are met.
All the demands were met.
The standard wasn't met, so I didn't pass.

examples.ko: 기본적인 욕구가 충족될 때 사람은 안정을 느껴요.
examples.en: People feel stable when their basic needs are fulfilled.
You can submit only when the requirements are met.

examples.ko: 충족된 상태에서도 더 바라는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people still want more even when they are satisfied.

explain: 충족되다는 조건, 기준, 요구, 욕구처럼 채워야 하는 것이 채워졌을 때 써요. 물건이 가득 찬 경우는 '채워지다'를 쓰고, 마음이 흡족한 것은 '만족하다'를 써요. 조건이 맞으면 충족되다, 마음이 흡족하면 만족하다로 구별하세요.
explain_en: 충족되다 is used when something that had to be filled, such as a condition, standard, demand or need, has been filled. A thing that fills up with objects is 채워지다, and being content in the heart is 만족하다. Use 충족되다 when conditions are met and 만족하다 when you feel content.

en: satisfy; fulfill; meet (a requirement or need)

examples.en: This product meets customers' needs.
I didn't meet the eligibility requirements, so I was rejected.
I want to satisfy my child's curiosity.

examples.ko: 조건을 모두 충족시키면 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you meet all the conditions, you can apply.

examples.ko: 새 가게는 다양한 입맛을 충족시키려고 메뉴를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The new shop added menu items to satisfy different tastes.

examples.ko: 기준을 충족시키는 후보가 한 명도 없었어요.
examples.en: There was not a single candidate who met the criteria.

explain: 충족시키다는 요구, 조건, 기대, 호기심에 맞게 해 준다는 쪽이라 목적어에 '요구, 조건, 기준, 욕구'가 와요. 말할 때는 '맞추다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. 배고픔을 채우는 것은 '채우다'를 써요.
explain_en: 충족시키다 goes with objects like demand, condition, criterion and desire, meaning to satisfy them. In speech 맞추다 is used more often. For filling hunger, the word is 채우다.

en: be circulated; spread (rumors, images, illegal material)

examples.en: Fake news was spread over the internet.
I was shocked that the rumor spread in no time.

examples.ko: 허락 없이 영상이 유포되는 건 문제예요.
examples.en: Having a video circulated without permission is a problem.

examples.ko: 잘못된 정보가 유포된 탓에 오해가 생겼어요.
examples.en: A misunderstanding arose because wrong information was circulated.
I asked for deletion before the photo got circulated.

examples.ko: 불법 자료가 유포되면 처벌을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If illegal material is circulated, you can be punished.

explain: 유포되다는 소문, 가짜 뉴스, 사진, 영상처럼 퍼지면 안 되거나 문제가 되는 것에 주로 써요. 좋은 소식이나 유행이 퍼질 때는 '퍼지다', '확산되다'가 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서 '불법 영상이 유포되다'처럼 많이 나와요.
explain_en: 유포되다 is mainly used for things that should not spread or cause problems: rumors, fake news, photos and videos. For good news or trends spreading, 퍼지다 or 확산되다 sounds natural. News often says things like 불법 영상이 유포되다.

en: circulate; spread (rumors, false information)

examples.en: That person spread a false rumor.

examples.ko: 친구의 사진을 허락 없이 유포하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not circulate a friend's photo without permission.
I reported the person who spreads fake news.

examples.ko: 거짓 정보를 유포한 혐의로 조사를 받고 있어요.
examples.en: He is being investigated on suspicion of spreading false information.
I don't know what the intention behind spreading the rumor was.
He apologized for circulating a post with an unclear source.

explain: 유포하다는 안 좋은 소문, 거짓 정보, 불법 자료를 퍼뜨릴 때 써서 대개 비난의 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서 소문을 퍼뜨리는 것은 '퍼뜨리다'가 자연스러워요. 좋은 뜻으로 알릴 때는 '알리다'를 써요.
explain_en: 유포하다 is used for spreading bad rumors, false information or illegal material, and it usually carries blame. In daily life, spreading a rumor is naturally 퍼뜨리다. To announce something in a good sense, use 알리다.

en: avoid; evade; dodge

examples.en: He dodged the question and didn't answer.
If you evade responsibility, you lose trust.
I hit the brakes hard to avoid an accident.

examples.ko: 눈을 마주치는 것을 회피하는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people avoid making eye contact.

examples.ko: 어려운 문제를 계속 회피할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't keep dodging a difficult problem.

examples.ko: 그는 갈등을 회피하다가 더 큰 문제를 만들었어요.
examples.en: He dodged the conflict and ended up creating a bigger problem.

explain: 회피하다는 책임, 질문, 갈등, 사람처럼 마주하기 싫은 것을 일부러 피할 때 써요. '피하다'는 비를 피하다처럼 넓게 쓰고, 회피하다는 일부러 마주하지 않는다는 비판적인 느낌이 있어요. 책임, 질문, 시선과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: 회피하다 is used when you deliberately stay away from something you don't want to face, such as responsibility, a question, a conflict or a person. 피하다 is broad, as in avoiding rain, while 회피하다 carries a critical feel of deliberately not facing it. It pairs well with responsibility, questions and eye contact.

en: be isolated; be quarantined; be separated

examples.en: The patient was isolated from other people.
Infected people are isolated in the hospital and get treatment.
That animal is kept separately.

examples.ko: 격리된 동안에는 가족도 만날 수 없어요.
examples.en: While in isolation, you can't even meet your family.

examples.ko: 열이 있는 학생은 잠시 다른 방에 격리돼요.
examples.en: A student with a fever is separated into another room for a while.
Once the accident site was sealed off from outside, it became quiet.

explain: 격리되다는 아픈 사람이나 위험한 것이 다른 사람과 떨어져 있도록 따로 두어질 때 써요. 병이나 사고 현장 이야기에 많이 나와요. 마음이 외롭게 끊겨 있는 상태는 '고립되다'가 가까워요.
explain_en: 격리되다 is used when a sick person or a dangerous thing is kept apart from others. It appears often in talk about illness or accident sites. For feeling lonely and cut off, 고립되다 is closer.

en: isolate; quarantine; separate

examples.en: The hospital isolated the patient in another room.
We have to isolate the patient to prevent infection.

examples.ko: 새로 들어온 고양이를 며칠 동안 격리하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to keep a new cat apart for a few days.

examples.ko: 선생님은 열이 있는 학생을 잠시 격리하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher separated the student with a fever for a while.

examples.ko: 사건 현장을 먼저 격리한 뒤 조사를 시작했어요.
examples.en: They sealed off the scene first and then started the investigation.
Keep dangerous items away from children.

explain: 격리하다는 위험하거나 전염될 수 있는 대상을 따로 떼어 두는 사람이나 기관이 주어예요. '~을/를 ~와/과 격리하다'로 써요. 벌을 주려고 가두는 것은 '가두다'이고, 격리하다는 보호나 예방이 목적이에요.
explain_en: In 격리하다 the subject is the person or institution that sets apart something dangerous or contagious. The pattern is ~을/를 ~와/과 격리하다. Locking someone up as punishment is 가두다; 격리하다 aims at protection or prevention.

en: be rescued; be freed

examples.ko: 산에서 길을 잃은 사람이 무사히 구출되었어요.
examples.en: A person lost in the mountains was rescued safely.
The child was rescued from the burning building.
The rescued puppy met a new family.

examples.ko: 갇혀 있던 사람들이 하루 만에 구출될 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The people who were trapped could be rescued within a day.

examples.ko: 배에 있던 승객이 모두 구출돼서 안심했어요.
examples.en: I felt relieved that all the passengers on the ship were rescued.
The moment they were rescued from danger, everyone cheered.

explain: 구출되다는 위험하거나 갇힌 곳에서 도움을 받아 빠져나올 때 써요. 사고, 화재, 납치처럼 급한 상황이 떠오르는 말이에요. '구조되다'는 재난에서 도움을 받는 쪽에, 구출되다는 갇힌 곳에서 빼내지는 쪽에 가까운데 실제로는 거의 겹쳐서 써요.
explain_en: 구출되다 is used when someone gets out of a dangerous or confined place with help. It brings to mind urgent situations such as accidents, fires or kidnappings. 구조되다 leans toward being helped in a disaster and 구출되다 toward being pulled out of confinement, but in practice they overlap a lot.

en: rescue; save; free

examples.en: A firefighter rescued a child from the burning house.

examples.ko: 사람들이 물에 빠진 개를 구출하려고 뛰어들었어요.
examples.en: People jumped in to rescue the dog that fell in the water.

examples.ko: 우리는 눈에 갇힌 차를 구출하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to dig out the car stuck in the snow.

examples.ko: 영화 주인공이 친구를 구출하는 장면이 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The scene where the hero rescues his friend was cool.
I brought the rescued cat home.

examples.ko: 팀이 산에 갇힌 등산객을 구출했다고 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard the team rescued the hikers trapped in the mountains.

explain: 구출하다는 위험하거나 갇힌 곳에 있는 사람이나 동물을 직접 빼내 올 때 써요. 영화나 뉴스에 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '구해 주다'가 더 가볍게 쓰여요.
explain_en: 구출하다 is used when you directly bring a person or animal out of danger or confinement. It appears often in films and news, and in daily talk 구해 주다 is lighter.

en: retaliate; take revenge

examples.en: He took revenge on the friend who teased him.

examples.ko: 보복하려고 일부러 약속을 어긴 건 아니에요.
examples.en: I didn't break the promise on purpose to get back at him.

examples.ko: 상대 팀에게 보복하는 대신 경기에 집중했어요.
examples.en: Instead of retaliating against the other team, they focused on the game.
You must not retaliate just because someone reported you.

examples.ko: 보복할 기회를 기다리는 사람은 마음이 편하지 않아요.
examples.en: Someone waiting for a chance to get even is not at peace.

examples.ko: 보복하고 싶은 마음을 참은 게 잘한 일이에요.
examples.en: Holding back the urge to retaliate was the right thing.

explain: 보복하다는 복수하다와 비슷하지만 '보복 운전', '보복 범죄', '보복 관세'처럼 한 덩어리 말로도 많이 나와요. 대개 나쁜 행동에 나쁜 행동으로 되갚는다는 뜻이라 부정적인 느낌이 강해요. 신고한 사람에게 보복하는 일은 뉴스에서도 자주 다뤄요.
explain_en: 보복하다 is close to 복수하다, but it also appears a lot in set phrases such as 보복 운전 (road rage), 보복 범죄 and 보복 관세 (retaliatory tariff). It usually means paying back a bad act with another, so the feel is strongly negative. Retaliating against someone who reported you is a common news topic.

en: preach; give a sermon; lecture (someone) moralistically

examples.en: The pastor preaches every Sunday.

examples.ko: 아버지가 또 인생에 대해 설교하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My father started lecturing me about life again.
Don't lecture me.

examples.ko: 선배가 설교하는 말투로 말해서 듣기 싫었어요.
examples.en: The senior spoke in a preachy tone and I didn't want to listen.
At the church, the priest preached about forgiveness.

examples.ko: 친구는 내 잘못을 설교해서 기분이 상했어요.
examples.en: My friend lectured me about my mistake and I felt hurt.

explain: 설교하다는 원래 교회에서 종교 이야기를 전하는 일이에요. 일상에서는 윗사람이 길게 훈계하듯 말할 때 '설교하지 마'처럼 부정적으로 써요. '잔소리하다'는 짧게 반복되는 말, 설교하다는 길고 도덕적인 말이라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: 설교하다 originally refers to delivering a religious message at church. In daily life it is used negatively, as in 설교하지 마 ('don't preach at me'), when someone talks down at length. 잔소리하다 is short and repeated nagging, while 설교하다 is long and moralizing.

en: be achieved; be accomplished; come true

examples.en: My long-held dream was finally achieved.

examples.ko: 목표가 성취되면 상을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the goal is achieved, you can get a prize.
I prayed for my wish to come true.
Every plan was accomplished as planned.
I shared the achieved result with my teammates.
It took a long time until peace was achieved.

explain: 성취되다는 꿈, 목표, 소원, 평화처럼 큰 것이 이루어졌을 때 써요. 일상적인 일은 '이루어지다'가 자연스럽고, 성취되다는 오랜 노력 끝에 얻은 결과라는 느낌이에요. 스스로 해냈을 때는 '성취하다', 그때 느끼는 마음은 '성취감'이에요.
explain_en: 성취되다 is used when something big comes true, such as a dream, goal, wish or peace. For everyday matters 이루어지다 is more natural; 성취되다 feels like a result earned after long effort. When you did it yourself it is 성취하다, and the feeling you get is 성취감.

en: be suppressed; be oppressed; be held down

examples.en: In a society where freedom is suppressed, speaking up is hard.

examples.ko: 억압된 감정은 언젠가 다른 모습으로 나타나요.
examples.en: Suppressed emotions show up in another form someday.
When opinions are suppressed, ideas stop coming.
In those days, women's rights were suppressed.
The pent-up anger burst out all at once.
The more expression is suppressed, the more the discontent grows.

explain: 억압되다는 자유, 감정, 의견, 권리가 힘에 눌려 드러나지 못할 때 써요. 사회 이야기에도, 마음 이야기('억압된 감정')에도 모두 써요. 누르는 쪽은 '억압하다'예요. 스스로 참는 것은 '참다'를 써요.
explain_en: 억압되다 is used when freedom, emotions, opinions or rights are pressed down and cannot show. It works for society and for the mind, as in 억압된 감정. The pressing side is 억압하다. Holding something back by yourself is 참다.

en: suppress; oppress; hold down

examples.en: The dictator suppressed the people's freedom.

examples.ko: 부모가 아이의 감정을 억압하면 안 좋아요.
examples.en: It is bad when parents suppress their child's feelings.
He kept his discontent down and finally exploded.

examples.ko: 말을 못 하게 억압하는 분위기가 싫었어요.
examples.en: I disliked the atmosphere that kept people from speaking.

examples.ko: 학교가 학생의 개성을 억압한다는 비판이 있어요.
examples.en: There is criticism that the school suppresses students' individuality.

examples.ko: 자신의 마음을 억압하지 말고 솔직하게 말하세요.
examples.en: Don't suppress your feelings; speak honestly.

explain: 억압하다는 힘이나 규칙으로 남의 자유, 말, 감정을 누를 때 써요. 자기 감정을 스스로 누를 때도 쓸 수 있지만 이때는 '참다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 정치와 사회 이야기에서 많이 나오고 비판하는 뜻이 강해요.
explain_en: 억압하다 is used when someone presses down another's freedom, speech or feelings by force or rules. It can also describe holding down your own feelings, but 참다 is far more natural there. It appears a lot in political and social talk and carries strong criticism.

en: toxic; poisonous

examples.ko: 이 버섯은 유독해서 먹으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This mushroom is poisonous, so you must not eat it.
Toxic gas leaked out of the factory.

examples.ko: 유독한 물질은 아이들 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep toxic substances out of children's reach.
They say the leaves of this plant are poisonous.

examples.ko: 창문을 열어서 유독한 연기가 나가게 했어요.
examples.en: I opened the window to let the toxic smoke out.
In the lab, we used only non-toxic chemicals.

explain: 유독하다는 화학 물질, 가스, 버섯, 식물이 사람에게 해로울 때 써요. 부사 '유독'(특히)과 소리가 같으니 문장에서 구별하세요. 말할 때는 '독성이 있다'가 더 자주 들려요. 반대는 '무독하다'예요.
explain_en: 유독하다 is used when a chemical, gas, mushroom or plant is harmful to people. It sounds like the adverb 유독 (especially), so tell them apart in the sentence. In speech 독성이 있다 is heard more often. The opposite is 무독하다.

en: be demolished; be torn down; be removed

examples.en: The old building was demolished.
All the signs beside the road were taken down.

examples.ko: 불법 건물은 다음 달에 철거될 예정이에요.
examples.en: The illegal building is set to be torn down next month.
A park will be built where it was demolished.

examples.ko: 낡은 아파트가 철거되는 동안 소음이 심했어요.
examples.en: The noise was bad while the old apartment was being demolished.
As the tents were removed, the square became spacious again.

explain: 철거되다는 건물, 시설, 간판처럼 세워져 있던 것이 치워져 없어질 때 써요. 철거 현장, 철거 공사 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 물건을 정리해서 버리는 '치우다'와 달리 구조물을 뜯어낸다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 철거되다 is used when something that stood, such as a building, facility or sign, is cleared away. It appears with words like 철거 현장 and 철거 공사. Unlike 치우다, which means tidying things away, it feels like tearing down a structure.

en: demolish; tear down; remove

examples.en: City Hall removed the illegal signs.

examples.ko: 낡은 건물을 철거하는 데 한 달이 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a month to demolish an old building.
The event is over, so we have to take down the stage.

examples.ko: 가게 앞 천막을 철거하라는 안내문이 붙었어요.
examples.en: A notice was posted ordering the awning in front of the shop removed.
Residents demanded that the construction site be removed.

examples.ko: 이사 전에 에어컨을 철거할 업체를 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found a company to take down the air conditioner before the move.

explain: 철거하다는 건물, 천막, 간판, 설비처럼 설치된 것을 뜯어서 없앨 때 써요. 설치하다, 세우다의 반대편에 있는 말이에요. 에어컨 같은 작은 설비에도 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서는 '떼다'나 '뜯다'가 더 흔해요.
explain_en: 철거하다 is used for taking apart and removing something installed, such as a building, awning, sign or equipment. It is the counterpart of 설치하다 and 세우다. It is also used for small equipment like an air conditioner, but daily speech uses 떼다 or 뜯다 more often.
